// diagnostic

E0170

This range counts the wrong way for its written ends

What

This range counts the wrong way for its written ends

Why

A range without a step counts up, and a step that moves away from the end runs the loop zero times

Fix

Add the minus step (`10..1, -1`), flip the step's sign, or write the smaller end first

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0170: tests/ui/range_backward_written.stderr.

Error [jet.DynAsCondition]: This range counts down from 10 to 1 but has no step
  --> tests/ui/range_backward_written.jet:3:15
    |
  3 |     loop i in 10..1 { print(i) }
    |               ^^^^^
 Why: A range without a step counts up, so `10..1` would run zero times
 Fix: Add the minus step: `10..1, -1`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0170

Error [jet.DynAsCondition]: This range counts up from 0 to 10 but its step -1 counts down
  --> tests/ui/range_backward_written.jet:4:22
    |
  4 |     loop j in 0..10, -1 { print(j) }
    |                      ^^
 Why: A negative step moves away from 10, so the loop would run zero times
 Fix: Make the step positive: `0..10, 1`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0170

Error [jet.DynAsCondition]: This range counts down from 10 to 0 but its step 2 counts up
  --> tests/ui/range_backward_written.jet:5:22
    |
  5 |     loop k in 10..0, 2 { print(k) }
    |                      ^
 Why: A positive step moves away from 0, so the loop would run zero times
 Fix: Make the step negative: `10..0, -2`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0170

Error [jet.DynAsCondition]: This range counts down from 5 to 2 and holds no numbers
  --> tests/ui/range_backward_written.jet:6:13
    |
  6 |     window: 5..<2
    |             ^^^^^
 Why: A range value always counts up from its start, so a bigger start leaves it empty
 Fix: Write the smaller end first, `2..<5`; count down in a loop with `5..<2, -1`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0170
